pairs.subject: model-call-outcome-integrity
pairs.evidence: packages/kernel/src/router/reserve.ts:125 The persisted `router.refused` event's `reason` field normally carries a `RefusalReason` member (reserve.ts:109), but here a literal "over-budget" is written at the call site even though the one owning union (types.ts:181) does not contain it, so anything that groups or alerts on refusal reasons meets a value the vocabulary does not declare.

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/src/router/types.ts:181 Most of this is realized: the `Why` union is closed, the trail rides on both Routed and Refused, and routed/refused events persist the same trail values. But the `over-budget` refusal cause is a special-cased string in reserve.ts:125 instead of a member of this set, which is the failure the rule names ('never a special-cased string at a call site').

packages/kernel/src/router/route.ts:153 Calls are keyed by capability/turn class from the closed TURN_CLASSES list (tables.ts:149), and an unclassified call is refused, never defaulted. routeAndReserve also requires `subject` in its input (reserve.ts:87). Caveat: `class` is optional in RouteRequest, so the check runs when the request is routed, not at compile time.

packages/kernel/src/router/reserve.ts:138 The precondition holds: the text local plan has the claude-cli seat and metered google serving the same turns (tables.ts:224). Posture comes from a configured env map, and a malformed value fails (posture.ts). The lane that paid (seat.text vs cloud.google) is written on every routed event. Building the child-process environment and stripping credentials happen in the driver, outside this context, and were not judged.

packages/kernel/src/router/types.ts:91 Timeout, cancelled and refused are kept apart from bad-response. Never-reached outcomes are Refused values (absent/exhausted), separate from `stopped` after a real attempt. A missing pace is `seconds: null`, not zero. Calibration returns `insufficient` with no AUC rather than a number (core.ts:83).

packages/kernel/src/calibration/series.ts:28 The calibration series is keyed by the served grader's model and schema/prompt digest, so scores from two configurations never pool. Registering the same key with a different value is a conflict (series.ts:76). Only operator verdicts count as labels. Weak spot: series.ts:68 checks only that the series string is non-empty; nothing checks that it carries the digest.

packages/kernel/src/router/reserve.ts:15 This context reserves before any call and never sees a response, so there is no failed-after-spend path whose ledger/raise order it could get wrong. Settlement happens in the driver.
packages/kernel/src/router/route.ts:29 The router is pure and translates no structured-output contract into a vendor dialect.
packages/kernel/src/router/route.ts:48 The retry/reroute ladder and its deadline live in the driver. The router only refuses to walk past a timeout and holds no clock or deadline.
